independence_basis: separate process, fresh session, clean checkout, integrity verified

findings.evidence: conftest imports uri_core.app.server while the placeholders are installed, then deletes only google*/googleapiclient*/google_auth_* entries from sys.modules. uri_core.app.server and uri_core.services.gmail_service (etc.) remain imported with MagicMock bindings: a probe test run after tests/graphify sees type(uri_core.services.gmail_service.build) == MagicMock. Repro on this host (Google packages not installed): `pytest tests/test_m31_model_brain_ux.py` -> 1 collection error; `pytest tests/graphify tests/test_m31_model_brain_ux.py` -> 25 passed. Same for test_decision_engine.py (error alone; 60 passed with tests/graphify). tests/graphify sorts before tests/test_* in a plain `pytest tests` run. os.environ.setdefault('URI_EXTERNAL_CREDENTIAL_SECRET', ...) at module level also persists for the session. This contradicts the conftest docstring ('no other test in the same run can see them') and review focus 5.
findings.suggested_fix: Isolate the placeholder import: snapshot sys.modules before it and, on teardown of tests/graphify (session/module fixture or pytest_unconfigure-scoped hook), remove every module added during the placeholder window (including uri_core.*), or use pytest.importorskip / run the tests in a subprocess. Set the credential secret with monkeypatch inside a fixture rather than at import time.
findings.title: conftest placeholders leak into other tests in the same run (server and uri_core.services stay bound to MagicMock Google modules; credential secret persists)

findings.evidence: _sync_memory calls graphify_index.refresh(scope='memory'), which deletes then re-adds keys in self.records in place, on every get/list_all/relevant_subset. /ask is a sync endpoint, so FastAPI runs it in its thread pool; the no-login view is shared by all no-login requests. Probe (/tmp/uri_review_R1/conc/test_conc.py; 300 memories, sys.setswitchinterval(1e-6)): two threads calling view.relevant_subset raise KeyError('memory:...') out of relevant_subset (the error comes from _sync_memory, outside relevant_subset's own try). With list_all readers: RuntimeError 'dictionary changed size during iteration'. A concurrent refresh(view, scope='capabilities') (as in refresh_user_external_lifecycle, server.py:665) raised RuntimeError 1466 times in 8 s; external_lifecycle_lock does not cover Brain-turn lookups, so a capability republish can abort before multi_action_dispatch is swapped. decision_engine catches the relevant_subset error, so in a Brain turn this drops the hint for that turn. Before this change, lookups only read.
findings.suggested_fix: Build the merged record dict (non-memory plus freshly indexed memory) in a local variable and assign self.records once, under a per-view lock that the capability/service refresh path also takes (or have that refresh replace records atomically under the same lock). Catch any exception in _sync_memory so a lookup never raises.
findings.title: Lookups edit the view's shared records without a lock: concurrent lookups and the capability refresh raise KeyError/RuntimeError
